## Goal — a dispatched fork leg actually works the PR head tree (v1)

One sentence: **the leg's checkout consumes `inputs.checkout_ref`** — a gh-1075 fork-PR dispatch rides the base machine ref (`main`) and carries `refs/pull/<N>/head` in `inputs.checkout_ref`; the leg's checkout step must resolve that ref instead of the dispatch ref, so review/rework legs examine the fork PR's actual changes — not the base tree.

## Why this card exists (gh-1075 review thread, round 2)

gh-1075 (#1075 / PR #1089) made cross-repo PRs dispatchable: the dispatch reroutes onto `main` and DECLARES `checkout_ref` in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (declaration was required — GitHub 422s undeclared dispatch inputs, github/gh-aw#50027). Consumption was deferred, and the deferral named the #1074 lane. Review verified against the #1074 card text: #1074 is scoped **failure observability only** ("Non-goals: changing failure semantics") — it does NOT own a checkout-behavior change. So the consumption has no owner until this card.

The failure mode without it is silent wrong-tree work: a fork leg checks out `main`, produces green review/rework runs against the base code, and the fork PR's actual changes are never examined — no error anywhere (AC1 of gh-1075 "the leg's checkout step resolves refs/pull/<N>/head" stays unmet end-to-end).

## Scope

- The **template** `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` checkout step: when `inputs.checkout_ref != ''`, check out that ref (`git fetch origin <checkout_ref> && git checkout FETCH_HEAD`, or `gh pr checkout <N>`) instead of the dispatch ref. The placeholder `teammate` job documents the adaptation point; the machine-kit reference workflow (epam/dmtools-dart) carries the working runner steps and needs the same change.
- The **self-host stub** path: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` delegates to `IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml` — the factory reusable workflow must declare a `checkout_ref` input and consume it in its checkout step (sibling repo change; track here).
- The **rework push-back** targets the fork per the gh-1070 maintainer-edit contract (push to the fork's token URL, never the base branch).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A leg dispatched with `inputs.checkout_ref = refs/pull/<N>/head` checks out the PR head sha; the leg's git ops (diff, review, rework edits) run against the fork head tree.
- **AC2** — Same-repo dispatches (no `checkout_ref`) are byte-identical: checkout resolves the dispatch ref as today (REG guard).
- **AC3** — The rework leg's push-back lands on the fork (gh-1070 `forkPushTokenUrl` idiom), and a lint/unit assertion pins the checkout consumption so a future template edit cannot silently drop it (the way `test_forkDispatch.js` pins the declaration).
- **AC4** — The factory reusable workflow declares `checkout_ref` (no undeclared `with:` input — GitHub fails reusable-workflow calls with unexpected inputs).

- UT-1: template lint — the checkout step references `github.event.inputs.checkout_ref` and is guarded by `!= ''`.
- UT-2: a rendered checkout command for a fork dispatch names `refs/pull/<N>/head`.
- REG-1: existing gh-1075 fork-dispatch suites (dispatch reroute, probe, park) stay green.

- The gh-1075 dispatch reroute itself (merged in PR #1089).
- The `validate_pr` CI-lane fork reroute (fork-blind lane; tracked separately, see the gh-1075 AC2 fork-blind notice).

One sentence: **the leg's checkout consumes `inputs.checkout_ref`** — a gh-1075 fork-PR dispatch rides the base machine ref (`main`) and carries `refs/pull/<N>/head` in `inputs.checkout_ref`; the leg's checkout step must resolve that ref instead of the dispatch ref, so review/rework legs examine the fork PR's actual changes — not the base tree.

## Why this card exists (gh-1075 review thread, round 2)

gh-1075 (#1075 / PR #1089) made cross-repo PRs dispatchable: the dispatch reroutes onto `main` and DECLARES `checkout_ref` in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (declaration was required — GitHub 422s undeclared dispatch inputs, github/gh-aw#50027). So the consumption has no owner until this card.

The failure mode without it is silent wrong-tree work: a fork leg checks out `main`, produces green review/rework runs against the base code, and the fork PR's actual changes are never examined — no error anywhere (AC1 of gh-1075 "the leg's checkout step resolves refs/pull/<N>/head" stays unmet end-to-end).

## Scope

- The **template** `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` checkout step: when `inputs.checkout_ref != ''`, check out that ref (`git fetch origin <checkout_ref> && git checkout FETCH_HEAD`, or `gh pr checkout <N>`) instead of the dispatch ref. gh-1075 (#1075 / PR #1089) made cross-repo PRs dispatchable: the dispatch reroutes onto `main` and DECLARES `checkout_ref` in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (declaration was required — GitHub 422s undeclared dispatch inputs, github/gh-aw#50027). ## Goal — a dispatched fork leg actually works the PR head tree (v1)

One sentence: **the leg's checkout consumes `inputs.checkout_ref`** — a gh-1075 fork-PR dispatch rides the base machine ref (`main`) and carries `refs/pull/<N>/head` in `inputs.checkout_ref`; the leg's checkout step must resolve that ref instead of the dispatch ref, so review/rework legs examine the fork PR's actual changes — not the base tree.

## Why this card exists (gh-1075 review thread, round 2)

gh-1075 (#1075 / PR #1089) made cross-repo PRs dispatchable: the dispatch reroutes onto `main` and DECLARES `checkout_ref` in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (declaration was required — GitHub 422s undeclared dispatch inputs, github/gh-aw#50027). Consumption was deferred, and the deferral named the #1074 lane. Review verified against the #1074 card text: #1074 is scoped **failure observability only** ("Non-goals: changing failure semantics") — it does NOT own a checkout-behavior change. So the consumption has no owner until this card.

The failure mode without it is silent wrong-tree work: a fork leg checks out `main`, produces green review/rework runs against the base code, and the fork PR's actual changes are never examined — no error anywhere (AC1 of gh-1075 "the leg's checkout step resolves refs/pull/<N>/head" stays unmet end-to-end).

## Scope

- The **template** `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` checkout step: when `inputs.checkout_ref != ''`, check out that ref (`git fetch origin <checkout_ref> && git checkout FETCH_HEAD`, or `gh pr checkout <N>`) instead of the dispatch ref. - The **rework push-back** targets the fork per the gh-1070 maintainer-edit contract (push to the fork's token URL, never the base branch).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A leg dispatched with `inputs.checkout_ref = refs/pull/<N>/head` checks out the PR head sha; the leg's git ops (diff, review, rework edits) run against the fork head tree.

## Goal — a dispatched fork leg actually works the PR head tree (v1)

One sentence: **the leg's checkout consumes `inputs.checkout_ref`** — a gh-1075 fork-PR dispatch rides the base machine ref (`main`) and carries `refs/pull/<N>/head` in `inputs.checkout_ref`; the leg's checkout step must resolve that ref instead of the dispatch ref, so review/rework legs examine the fork PR's actual changes — not the base tree.

## Why this card exists (gh-1075 review thread, round 2)

gh-1075 (#1075 / PR #1089) made cross-repo PRs dispatchable: the dispatch reroutes onto `main` and DECLARES `checkout_ref` in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (declaration was required — GitHub 422s undeclared dispatch inputs, github/gh-aw#50027). Consumption was deferred, and the deferral named the #1074 lane. Review verified against the #1074 card text: #1074 is scoped **failure observability only** ("Non-goals: changing failure semantics") — it does NOT own a checkout-behavior change. So the consumption has no owner until this card.

The failure mode without it is silent wrong-tree work: a fork leg checks out `main`, produces green review/rework runs against the base code, and the fork PR's actual changes are never examined — no error anywhere (AC1 of gh-1075 "the leg's checkout step resolves refs/pull/<N>/head" stays unmet end-to-end).

## Scope

- The **template** `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` checkout step: when `inputs.checkout_ref != ''`, check out that ref (`git fetch origin <checkout_ref> && git checkout FETCH_HEAD`, or `gh pr checkout <N>`) instead of the dispatch ref. The placeholder `teammate` job documents the adaptation point; the machine-kit reference workflow (epam/dmtools-dart) carries the working runner steps and needs the same change.
- The **self-host stub** path: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` delegates to `IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml` — the factory reusable workflow must declare a `checkout_ref` input and consume it in its checkout step (sibling repo change; track here).
- The **rework push-back** targets the fork per the gh-1070 maintainer-edit contract (push to the fork's token URL, never the base branch).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A leg dispatched with `inputs.checkout_ref = refs/pull/<N>/head` checks out the PR head sha; the leg's git ops (diff, review, rework edits) run against the fork head tree.
- **AC2** — Same-repo dispatches (no `checkout_ref`) are byte-identical: checkout resolves the dispatch ref as today (REG guard).
- **AC3** — The rework leg's push-back lands on the fork (gh-1070 `forkPushTokenUrl` idiom), and a lint/unit assertion pins the checkout consumption so a future template edit cannot silently drop it (the way `test_forkDispatch.js` pins the declaration).
- **AC4** — The factory reusable workflow declares `checkout_ref` (no undeclared `with:` input — GitHub fails reusable-workflow calls with unexpected inputs).

- UT-1: template lint — the checkout step references `github.event.inputs.checkout_ref` and is guarded by `!= ''`.

- The `validate_pr` CI-lane fork reroute (fork-blind lane; tracked separately, see the gh-1075 AC2 fork-blind notice).

## Goal — a dispatched fork leg actually works the PR head tree (v1)

One sentence: **the leg's checkout consumes `inputs.checkout_ref`** — a gh-1075 fork-PR dispatch rides the base machine ref (`main`) and carries `refs/pull/<N>/head` in `inputs.checkout_ref`; the leg's checkout step must resolve that ref instead of the dispatch ref, so review/rework legs examine the fork PR's actual changes — not the base tree.

## Why this card exists (gh-1075 review thread, round 2)

gh-1075 (#1075 / PR #1089) made cross-repo PRs dispatchable: the dispatch reroutes onto `main` and DECLARES `checkout_ref` in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (declaration was required — GitHub 422s undeclared dispatch inputs, github/gh-aw#50027). Consumption was deferred, and the deferral named the #1074 lane. Review verified against the #1074 card text: #1074 is scoped **failure observability only** ("Non-goals: changing failure semantics") — it does NOT own a checkout-behavior change. So the consumption has no owner until this card.

The failure mode without it is silent wrong-tree work: a fork leg checks out `main`, produces green review/rework runs against the base code, and the fork PR's actual changes are never examined — no error anywhere (AC1 of gh-1075 "the leg's checkout step resolves refs/pull/<N>/head" stays unmet end-to-end).

## Scope

- The **template** `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` checkout step: when `inputs.checkout_ref != ''`, check out that ref (`git fetch origin <checkout_ref> && git checkout FETCH_HEAD`, or `gh pr checkout <N>`) instead of the dispatch ref. The placeholder `teammate` job documents the adaptation point; the machine-kit reference workflow (epam/dmtools-dart) carries the working runner steps and needs the same change.
- The **self-host stub** path: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` delegates to `IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml` — the factory reusable workflow must declare a `checkout_ref` input and consume it in its checkout step (sibling repo change; track here).
- The **rework push-back** targets the fork per the gh-1070 maintainer-edit contract (push to the fork's token URL, never the base branch).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A leg dispatched with `inputs.checkout_ref = refs/pull/<N>/head` checks out the PR head sha; the leg's git ops (diff, review, rework edits) run against the fork head tree.
- **AC2** — Same-repo dispatches (no `checkout_ref`) are byte-identical: checkout resolves the dispatch ref as today (REG guard).
- **AC3** — The rework leg's push-back lands on the fork (gh-1070 `forkPushTokenUrl` idiom), and a lint/unit assertion pins the checkout consumption so a future template edit cannot silently drop it (the way `test_forkDispatch.js` pins the declaration).
- **AC4** — The factory reusable workflow declares `checkout_ref` (no undeclared `with:` input — GitHub fails reusable-workflow calls with unexpected inputs).

## Goal — a dispatched fork leg actually works the PR head tree (v1)

One sentence: **the leg's checkout consumes `inputs.checkout_ref`** — a gh-1075 fork-PR dispatch rides the base machine ref (`main`) and carries `refs/pull/<N>/head` in `inputs.checkout_ref`; the leg's checkout step must resolve that ref instead of the dispatch ref, so review/rework legs examine the fork PR's actual changes — not the base tree.

## Why this card exists (gh-1075 review thread, round 2)

gh-1075 (#1075 / PR #1089) made cross-repo PRs dispatchable: the dispatch reroutes onto `main` and DECLARES `checkout_ref` in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (declaration was required — GitHub 422s undeclared dispatch inputs, github/gh-aw#50027). Consumption was deferred, and the deferral named the #1074 lane. Review verified against the #1074 card text: #1074 is scoped **failure observability only** ("Non-goals: changing failure semantics") — it does NOT own a checkout-behavior change. So the consumption has no owner until this card.

The failure mode without it is silent wrong-tree work: a fork leg checks out `main`, produces green review/rework runs against the base code, and the fork PR's actual changes are never examined — no error anywhere (AC1 of gh-1075 "the leg's checkout step resolves refs/pull/<N>/head" stays unmet end-to-end).

## Scope

- The **template** `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` checkout step: when `inputs.checkout_ref != ''`, check out that ref (`git fetch origin <checkout_ref> && git checkout FETCH_HEAD`, or `gh pr checkout <N>`) instead of the dispatch ref. The placeholder `teammate` job documents the adaptation point; the machine-kit reference workflow (epam/dmtools-dart) carries the working runner steps and needs the same change.
- The **self-host stub** path: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` delegates to `IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml` — the factory reusable workflow must declare a `checkout_ref` input and consume it in its checkout step (sibling repo change; track here).
- The **rework push-back** targets the fork per the gh-1070 maintainer-edit contract (push to the fork's token URL, never the base branch).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A leg dispatched with `inputs.checkout_ref = refs/pull/<N>/head` checks out the PR head sha; the leg's git ops (diff, review, rework edits) run against the fork head tree.
- **AC2** — Same-repo dispatches (no `checkout_ref`) are byte-identical: checkout resolves the dispatch ref as today (REG guard).
- **AC3** — The rework leg's push-back lands on the fork (gh-1070 `forkPushTokenUrl` idiom), and a lint/unit assertion pins the checkout consumption so a future template edit cannot silently drop it (the way `test_forkDispatch.js` pins the declaration).
- **AC4** — The factory reusable workflow declares `checkout_ref` (no undeclared `with:` input — GitHub fails reusable-workflow calls with unexpected inputs).

## Test plan

- UT-1: template lint — the checkout step references `github.event.inputs.checkout_ref` and is guarded by `!= ''`.
- UT-2: a rendered checkout command for a fork dispatch names `refs/pull/<N>/head`.
- REG-1: existing gh-1075 fork-dispatch suites (dispatch reroute, probe, park) stay green.

## Non-goals

- The gh-1075 dispatch reroute itself (merged in PR #1089).
- The `validate_pr` CI-lane fork reroute (fork-blind lane; tracked separately, see the gh-1075 AC2 fork-blind notice).

## Goal — a dispatched fork leg actually works the PR head tree (v1)

One sentence: **the leg's checkout consumes `inputs.checkout_ref`** — a gh-1075 fork-PR dispatch rides the base machine ref (`main`) and carries `refs/pull/<N>/head` in `inputs.checkout_ref`; the leg's checkout step must resolve that ref instead of the dispatch ref, so review/rework legs examine the fork PR's actual changes — not the base tree.

## Why this card exists (gh-1075 review thread, round 2)

gh-1075 (#1075 / PR #1089) made cross-repo PRs dispatchable: the dispatch reroutes onto `main` and DECLARES `checkout_ref` in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (declaration was required — GitHub 422s undeclared dispatch inputs, github/gh-aw#50027). Consumption was deferred, and the deferral named the #1074 lane. Review verified against the #1074 card text: #1074 is scoped **failure observability only** ("Non-goals: changing failure semantics") — it does NOT own a checkout-behavior change. So the consumption has no owner until this card.

The failure mode without it is silent wrong-tree work: a fork leg checks out `main`, produces green review/rework runs against the base code, and the fork PR's actual changes are never examined — no error anywhere (AC1 of gh-1075 "the leg's checkout step resolves refs/pull/<N>/head" stays unmet end-to-end).

## Scope

- The **template** `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` checkout step: when `inputs.checkout_ref != ''`, check out that ref (`git fetch origin <checkout_ref> && git checkout FETCH_HEAD`, or `gh pr checkout <N>`) instead of the dispatch ref. The placeholder `teammate` job documents the adaptation point; the machine-kit reference workflow (epam/dmtools-dart) carries the working runner steps and needs the same change.
- The **self-host stub** path: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` delegates to `IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml` — the factory reusable workflow must declare a `checkout_ref` input and consume it in its checkout step (sibling repo change; track here).
- The **rework push-back** targets the fork per the gh-1070 maintainer-edit contract (push to the fork's token URL, never the base branch).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A leg dispatched with `inputs.checkout_ref = refs/pull/<N>/head` checks out the PR head sha; the leg's git ops (diff, review, rework edits) run against the fork head tree.
- **AC2** — Same-repo dispatches (no `checkout_ref`) are byte-identical: checkout resolves the dispatch ref as today (REG guard).
- **AC3** — The rework leg's push-back lands on the fork (gh-1070 `forkPushTokenUrl` idiom), and a lint/unit assertion pins the checkout consumption so a future template edit cannot silently drop it (the way `test_forkDispatch.js` pins the declaration).
- **AC4** — The factory reusable workflow declares `checkout_ref` (no undeclared `with:` input — GitHub fails reusable-workflow calls with unexpected inputs).

- UT-1: template lint — the checkout step references `github.event.inputs.checkout_ref` and is guarded by `!= ''`.

gh-1075 (#1075 / PR #1089) made cross-repo PRs dispatchable: the dispatch reroutes onto `main` and DECLARES `checkout_ref` in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (declaration was required — GitHub 422s undeclared dispatch inputs, github/gh-aw#50027). The failure mode without it is silent wrong-tree work: a fork leg checks out `main`, produces green review/rework runs against the base code, and the fork PR's actual changes are never examined — no error anywhere (AC1 of gh-1075 "the leg's checkout step resolves refs/pull/<N>/head" stays unmet end-to-end).

## Scope

SWAP 44.=47:
+# gh-1076: the trailing `|| github.event.label.name` fallback is gone with
+# the labeled trigger — labeled events can no longer start this workflow,
+# and assigned/dispatch events resolve their leg from the labels above.
+# gh-1075: a PR-anchored dispatch ALSO carries the `· pr-<N>` anchor right
+# after the issue slot, BEFORE the leg — the gh-1075 fork path always
+# backfills inputs.pr, and the SM's pull-keyed leg probe
+# (branchLegGuard.hasActiveLegRunForPull) keys on this whole-token anchor
+# to suppress a second rework arm on the same fork PR. The anchor sits
+# BEFORE the trailing-leg token on purpose: stubTailLegOf (the teammate:
+# title family in legOfRunName) parses the leg at the END of the title,
+# and the gh-1065 completed-owner leg precision depends on it.
+run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format(' · pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) || '' }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && 'rework') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && 'review') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'pr_approved') && 'review') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:dev') && 'dev') || (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:develop') && 'dev') }}""}

## Goal — a dispatched fork leg actually works the PR head tree (v1)

One sentence: **the leg's checkout consumes `inputs.checkout_ref`** — a gh-1075 fork-PR dispatch rides the base machine ref (`main`) and carries `refs/pull/<N>/head` in `inputs.checkout_ref`; the leg's checkout step must resolve that ref instead of the dispatch ref, so review/rework legs examine the fork PR's actual changes — not the base tree.

## Why this card exists (gh-1075 review thread, round 2)

gh-1075 (#1075 / PR #1089) made cross-repo PRs dispatchable: the dispatch reroutes onto `main` and DECLARES `checkout_ref` in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (declaration was required — GitHub 422s undeclared dispatch inputs, github/gh-aw#50027). Consumption was deferred, and the deferral named the #1074 lane. Review verified against the #1074 card text: #1074 is scoped **failure observability only** ("Non-goals: changing failure semantics") — it does NOT own a checkout-behavior change. So the consumption has no owner until this card.

The failure mode without it is silent wrong-tree work: a fork leg checks out `main`, produces green review/rework runs against the base code, and the fork PR's actual changes are never examined — no error anywhere (AC1 of gh-1075 "the leg's checkout step resolves refs/pull/<N>/head" stays unmet end-to-end).

## Scope

- The **template** `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` checkout step: when `inputs.checkout_ref != ''`, check out that ref (`git fetch origin <checkout_ref> && git checkout FETCH_HEAD`, or `gh pr checkout <N>`) instead of the dispatch ref. The placeholder `teammate` job documents the adaptation point; the machine-kit reference workflow (epam/dmtools-dart) carries the working runner steps and needs the same change.
- The **self-host stub** path: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` delegates to `IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml` — the factory reusable workflow must declare a `checkout_ref` input and consume it in its checkout step (sibling repo change; track here).
- The **rework push-back** targets the fork per the gh-1070 maintainer-edit contract (push to the fork's token URL, never the base branch).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A leg dispatched with `inputs.checkout_ref = refs/pull/<N>/head` checks out the PR head sha; the leg's git ops (diff, review, rework edits) run against the fork head tree.
- **AC2** — Same-repo dispatches (no `checkout_ref`) are byte-identical: checkout resolves the dispatch ref as today (REG guard).
- **AC3** — The rework leg's push-back lands on the fork (gh-1070 `forkPushTokenUrl` idiom), and a lint/unit assertion pins the checkout consumption so a future template edit cannot silently drop it (the way `test_forkDispatch.js` pins the declaration).
- **AC4** — The factory reusable workflow declares `checkout_ref` (no undeclared `with:` input — GitHub fails reusable-workflow calls with unexpected inputs).

- UT-1: template lint — the checkout step references `github.event.inputs.checkout_ref` and is guarded by `!= ''`.
- UT-2: a rendered checkout command for a fork dispatch names `refs/pull/<N>/head`.
- REG-1: existing gh-1075 fork-dispatch suites (dispatch reroute, probe, park) stay green.

- The gh-1075 dispatch reroute itself (merged in PR #1089).
- The `validate_pr` CI-lane fork reroute (fork-blind lane; tracked separately, see the gh-1075 AC2 fork-blind notice).

## Goal — a dispatched fork leg actually works the PR head tree (v1)

One sentence: **the leg's checkout consumes `inputs.checkout_ref`** — a gh-1075 fork-PR dispatch rides the base machine ref (`main`) and carries `refs/pull/<N>/head` in `inputs.checkout_ref`; the leg's checkout step must resolve that ref instead of the dispatch ref, so review/rework legs examine the fork PR's actual changes — not the base tree.

## Why this card exists (gh-1075 review thread, round 2)

gh-1075 (#1075 / PR #1089) made cross-repo PRs dispatchable: the dispatch reroutes onto `main` and DECLARES `checkout_ref` in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (declaration was required — GitHub 422s undeclared dispatch inputs, github/gh-aw#50027). Consumption was deferred, and the deferral named the #1074 lane. Review verified against the #1074 card text: #1074 is scoped **failure observability only** ("Non-goals: changing failure semantics") — it does NOT own a checkout-behavior change. So the consumption has no owner until this card.

The failure mode without it is silent wrong-tree work: a fork leg checks out `main`, produces green review/rework runs against the base code, and the fork PR's actual changes are never examined — no error anywhere (AC1 of gh-1075 "the leg's checkout step resolves refs/pull/<N>/head" stays unmet end-to-end).

## Scope

- The **template** `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` checkout step: when `inputs.checkout_ref != ''`, check out that ref (`git fetch origin <checkout_ref> && git checkout FETCH_HEAD`, or `gh pr checkout <N>`) instead of the dispatch ref. The placeholder `teammate` job documents the adaptation point; the machine-kit reference workflow (epam/dmtools-dart) carries the working runner steps and needs the same change.
- The **self-host stub** path: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` delegates to `IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml` — the factory reusable workflow must declare a `checkout_ref` input and consume it in its checkout step (sibling repo change; track here).
- The **rework push-back** targets the fork per the gh-1070 maintainer-edit contract (push to the fork's token URL, never the base branch).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A leg dispatched with `inputs.checkout_ref = refs/pull/<N>/head` checks out the PR head sha; the leg's git ops (diff, review, rework edits) run against the fork head tree.
- **AC2** — Same-repo dispatches (no `checkout_ref`) are byte-identical: checkout resolves the dispatch ref as today (REG guard).
- **AC3** — The rework leg's push-back lands on the fork (gh-1070 `forkPushTokenUrl` idiom), and a lint/unit assertion pins the checkout consumption so a future template edit cannot silently drop it (the way `test_forkDispatch.js` pins the declaration).
- **AC4** — The factory reusable workflow declares `checkout_ref` (no undeclared `with:` input — GitHub fails reusable-workflow calls with unexpected inputs).

## Test plan

- UT-1: template lint — the checkout step references `github.event.inputs.checkout_ref` and is guarded by `!= ''`.
- UT-2: a rendered checkout command for a fork dispatch names `refs/pull/<N>/head`.
- REG-1: existing gh-1075 fork-dispatch suites (dispatch reroute, probe, park) stay green.

## Non-goals

- The gh-1075 dispatch reroute itself (merged in PR #1089).
- The `validate_pr` CI-lane fork reroute (fork-blind lane; tracked separately, see the gh-1075 AC2 fork-blind notice).

## Live context

## Goal — a dispatched fork leg actually works the PR head tree (v1)

One sentence: **the leg's checkout consumes `inputs.checkout_ref`** — a gh-1075 fork-PR dispatch rides the base machine ref (`main`) and carries `refs/pull/<N>/head` in `inputs.checkout_ref`; the leg's checkout step must resolve that ref instead of the dispatch ref, so review/rework legs examine the fork PR's actual changes — not the base tree.

## Why this card exists (gh-1075 review thread, round 2)

gh-1075 (#1075 / PR #1089) made cross-repo PRs dispatchable: the dispatch reroutes onto `main` and DECLARES `checkout_ref` in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (declaration was required — GitHub 422s undeclared dispatch inputs, github/gh-aw#50027). Consumption was deferred, and the deferral named the #1074 lane. Review verified against the #1074 card text: #1074 is scoped **failure observability only** ("Non-goals: changing failure semantics") — it does NOT own a checkout-behavior change. So the consumption has no owner until this card.

The failure mode without it is silent wrong-tree work: a fork leg checks out `main`, produces green review/rework runs against the base code, and the fork PR's actual changes are never examined — no error anywhere (AC1 of gh-1075 "the leg's checkout step resolves refs/pull/<N>/head" stays unmet end-to-end).

## Scope

- The **template** `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` checkout step: when `inputs.checkout_ref != ''`, check out that ref (`git fetch origin <checkout_ref> && git checkout FETCH_HEAD`, or `gh pr checkout <N>`) instead of the dispatch ref. - The **self-host stub** path: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` delegates to `IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml` — the factory reusable workflow must declare a `checkout_ref` input and consume it in its checkout step (sibling repo change; track here).
- The **rework push-back** targets the fork per the gh-1070 maintainer-edit contract (push to the fork's token URL, never the base branch).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A leg dispatched with `inputs.checkout_ref = refs/pull/<N>/head` checks out the PR head sha; the leg's git ops (diff, review, rework edits) run against the fork head tree.
- **AC2** — Same-repo dispatches (no `checkout_ref`) are byte-identical: checkout resolves the dispatch ref as today (REG guard).
- **AC3** — The rework leg's push-back lands on the fork (gh-1070 `forkPushTokenUrl` idiom), and a lint/unit assertion pins the checkout consumption so a future template edit cannot silently drop it (the way `test_forkDispatch.js` pins the declaration).
- **AC4** — The factory reusable workflow declares `checkout_ref` (no undeclared `with:` input — GitHub fails reusable-workflow calls with unexpected inputs).

## Goal — a dispatched fork leg actually works the PR head tree (v1)

One sentence: **the leg's checkout consumes `inputs.checkout_ref`** — a gh-1075 fork-PR dispatch rides the base machine ref (`main`) and carries `refs/pull/<N>/head` in `inputs.checkout_ref`; the leg's checkout step must resolve that ref instead of the dispatch ref, so review/rework legs examine the fork PR's actual changes — not the base tree.

## Why this card exists (gh-1075 review thread, round 2)

gh-1075 (#1075 / PR #1089) made cross-repo PRs dispatchable: the dispatch reroutes onto `main` and DECLARES `checkout_ref` in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (declaration was required — GitHub 422s undeclared dispatch inputs, github/gh-aw#50027). Consumption was deferred, and the deferral named the #1074 lane. Review verified against the #1074 card text: #1074 is scoped **failure observability only** ("Non-goals: changing failure semantics") — it does NOT own a checkout-behavior change. So the consumption has no owner until this card.

The failure mode without it is silent wrong-tree work: a fork leg checks out `main`, produces green review/rework runs against the base code, and the fork PR's actual changes are never examined — no error anywhere (AC1 of gh-1075 "the leg's checkout step resolves refs/pull/<N>/head" stays unmet end-to-end).

## Scope

- The **template** `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` checkout step: when `inputs.checkout_ref != ''`, check out that ref (`git fetch origin <checkout_ref> && git checkout FETCH_HEAD`, or `gh pr checkout <N>`) instead of the dispatch ref. The placeholder `teammate` job documents the adaptation point; the machine-kit reference workflow (epam/dmtools-dart) carries the working runner steps and needs the same change.
- The **self-host stub** path: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` delegates to `IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml` — the factory reusable workflow must declare a `checkout_ref` input and consume it in its checkout step (sibling repo change; track here).
- The **rework push-back** targets the fork per the gh-1070 maintainer-edit contract (push to the fork's token URL, never the base branch).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A leg dispatched with `inputs.checkout_ref = refs/pull/<N>/head` checks out the PR head sha; the leg's git ops (diff, review, rework edits) run against the fork head tree.
- **AC2** — Same-repo dispatches (no `checkout_ref`) are byte-identical: checkout resolves the dispatch ref as today (REG guard).
- **AC3** — The rework leg's push-back lands on the fork (gh-1070 `forkPushTokenUrl` idiom), and a lint/unit assertion pins the checkout consumption so a future template edit cannot silently drop it (the way `test_forkDispatch.js` pins the declaration).
- **AC4** — The factory reusable workflow declares `checkout_ref` (no undeclared `with:` input — GitHub fails reusable-workflow calls with unexpected inputs).

## Test plan

- UT-1: template lint — the checkout step references `github.event.inputs.checkout_ref` and is guarded by `!= ''`.
- UT-2: a rendered checkout command for a fork dispatch names `refs/pull/<N>/head`.
- REG-1: existing gh-1075 fork-dispatch suites (dispatch reroute, probe, park) stay green.

## Non-goals

- The gh-1075 dispatch reroute itself (merged in PR #1089).
- The `validate_pr` CI-lane fork reroute (fork-blind lane; tracked separately, see the gh-1075 AC2 fork-blind notice).

## Live context

## Goal — a dispatched fork leg actually works the PR head tree (v1)

One sentence: **the leg's checkout consumes `inputs.checkout_ref`** — a gh-1075 fork-PR dispatch rides the base machine ref (`main`) and carries `refs/pull/<N>/head` in `inputs.checkout_ref`; the leg's checkout step must resolve that ref instead of the dispatch ref, so review/rework legs examine the fork PR's actual changes — not the base tree.

## Why this card exists (gh-1075 review thread, round 2)

gh-1075 (#1075 / PR #1089) made cross-repo PRs dispatchable: the dispatch reroutes onto `main` and DECLARES `checkout_ref` in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (declaration was required — GitHub 422s undeclared dispatch inputs, github/gh-aw#50027). Consumption was deferred, and the deferral named the #1074 lane. Review verified against the #1074 card text: #1074 is scoped **failure observability only** ("Non-goals: changing failure semantics") — it does NOT own a checkout-behavior change. So the consumption has no owner until this card.

The failure mode without it is silent wrong-tree work: a fork leg checks out `main`, produces green review/rework runs against the base code, and the fork PR's actual changes are never examined — no error anywhere (AC1 of gh-1075 "the leg's checkout step resolves refs/pull/<N>/head" stays unmet end-to-end).

## Scope

- The **template** `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` checkout step: when `inputs.checkout_ref != ''`, check out that ref (`git fetch origin <checkout_ref> && git checkout FETCH_HEAD`, or `gh pr checkout <N>`) instead of the dispatch ref. - The **self-host stub** path: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` delegates to `IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml` — the factory reusable workflow must declare a `checkout_ref` input and consume it in its checkout step (sibling repo change; track here).
- The **rework push-back** targets the fork per the gh-1070 maintainer-edit contract (push to the fork's token URL, never the base branch).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A leg dispatched with `inputs.checkout_ref = refs/pull/<N>/head` checks out the PR head sha; the leg's git ops (diff, review, rework edits) run against the fork head tree.
- **AC2** — Same-repo dispatches (no `checkout_ref`) are byte-identical: checkout resolves the dispatch ref as today (REG guard).
- **AC3** — The rework leg's push-back lands on the fork (gh-1070 `forkPushTokenUrl` idiom), and a lint/unit assertion pins the checkout consumption so a future template edit cannot silently drop it (the way `test_forkDispatch.js` pins the declaration).
- **AC4** — The factory reusable workflow declares `checkout_ref` (no undeclared `with:` input — GitHub fails reusable-workflow calls with unexpected inputs).

## Goal — a dispatched fork leg actually works the PR head tree (v1)

One sentence: **the leg's checkout consumes `inputs.checkout_ref`** — a gh-1075 fork-PR dispatch rides the base machine ref (`main`) and carries `refs/pull/<N>/head` in `inputs.checkout_ref`; the leg's checkout step must resolve that ref instead of the dispatch ref, so review/rework legs examine the fork PR's actual changes — not the base tree.

## Why this card exists (gh-1075 review thread, round 2)

gh-1075 (#1075 / PR #1089) made cross-repo PRs dispatchable: the dispatch reroutes onto `main` and DECLARES `checkout_ref` in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (declaration was required — GitHub 422s undeclared dispatch inputs, github/gh-aw#50027). Consumption was deferred, and the deferral named the #1074 lane. Review verified against the #1074 card text: #1074 is scoped **failure observability only** ("Non-goals: changing failure semantics") — it does NOT own a checkout-behavior change. So the consumption has no owner until this card.

The failure mode without it is silent wrong-tree work: a fork leg checks out `main`, produces green review/rework runs against the base code, and the fork PR's actual changes are never examined — no error anywhere (AC1 of gh-1075 "the leg's checkout step resolves refs/pull/<N>/head" stays unmet end-to-end).

## Scope

- The **template** `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` checkout step: when `inputs.checkout_ref != ''`, check out that ref (`git fetch origin <checkout_ref> && git checkout FETCH_HEAD`, or `gh pr checkout <N>`) instead of the dispatch ref. The placeholder `teammate` job documents the adaptation point; the machine-kit reference workflow (epam/dmtools-dart) carries the working runner steps and needs the same change.
- The **self-host stub** path: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` delegates to `IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml` — the factory reusable workflow must declare a `checkout_ref` input and consume it in its checkout step (sibling repo change; track here).
- The **rework push-back** targets the fork per the gh-1070 maintainer-edit contract (push to the fork's token URL, never the base branch).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A leg dispatched with `inputs.checkout_ref = refs/pull/<N>/head` checks out the PR head sha; the leg's git ops (diff, review, rework edits) run against the fork head tree.
- **AC2** — Same-repo dispatches (no `checkout_ref`) are byte-identical: checkout resolves the dispatch ref as today (REG guard).
- **AC3** — The rework leg's push-back lands on the fork (gh-1070 `forkPushTokenUrl` idiom), and a lint/unit assertion pins the checkout consumption so a future template edit cannot silently drop it (the way `test_forkDispatch.js` pins the declaration).
- **AC4** — The factory reusable workflow declares `checkout_ref` (no undeclared `with:` input — GitHub fails reusable-workflow calls with unexpected inputs).

## Test plan

- UT-1: template lint — the checkout step references `github.event.inputs.checkout_ref` and is guarded by `!= ''`.
- UT-2: a rendered checkout command for a fork dispatch names `refs/pull/<N>/head`.
- REG-1: existing gh-1075 fork-dispatch suites (dispatch reroute, probe, park) stay green.

## Non-goals

- The gh-1075 dispatch reroute itself (merged in PR #1089).
- The `validate_pr` CI-lane fork reroute (fork-blind lane; tracked separately, see the gh-1075 AC2 fork-blind notice).

## Live context

## Goal — a dispatched fork leg actually works the PR head tree (v1)

One sentence: **the leg's checkout consumes `inputs.checkout_ref`** — a gh-1075 fork-PR dispatch rides the base machine ref (`main`) and carries `refs/pull/<N>/head` in `inputs.checkout_ref`; the leg's checkout step must resolve that ref instead of the dispatch ref, so review/rework legs examine the fork PR's actual changes — not the base tree.

## Why this card exists (gh-1075 review thread, round 2)

gh-1075 (#1075 / PR #1089) made cross-repo PRs dispatchable: the dispatch reroutes onto `main` and DECLARES `checkout_ref` in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (declaration was required — GitHub 422s undeclared dispatch inputs, github/gh-aw#50027). Consumption was deferred, and the deferral named the #1074 lane. Review verified against the #1074 card text: #1074 is scoped **failure observability only** ("Non-goals: changing failure semantics") — it does NOT own a checkout-behavior change. So the consumption has no owner until this card.

The failure mode without it is silent wrong-tree work: a fork leg checks out `main`, produces green review/rework runs against the base code, and the fork PR's actual changes are never examined — no error anywhere (AC1 of gh-1075 "the leg's checkout step resolves refs/pull/<N>/head" stays unmet end-to-end).

## Scope

- The **template** `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` checkout step: when `inputs.checkout_ref != ''`, check out that ref (`git fetch origin <checkout_ref> && git checkout FETCH_HEAD`, or `gh pr checkout <N>`) instead of the dispatch ref. - The **self-host stub** path: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` delegates to `IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml` — the factory reusable workflow must declare a `checkout_ref` input and consume it in its checkout step (sibling repo change; track here).
- The **rework push-back** targets the fork per the gh-1070 maintainer-edit contract (push to the fork's token URL, never the base branch).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A leg dispatched with `inputs.checkout_ref = refs/pull/<N>/head` checks out the PR head sha; the leg's git ops (diff, review, rework edits) run against the fork head tree.
- **AC2** — Same-repo dispatches (no `checkout_ref`) are byte-identical: checkout resolves the dispatch ref as today (REG guard).
- **AC3** — The rework leg's push-back lands on the fork (gh-1070 `forkPushTokenUrl` idiom), and a lint/unit assertion pins the checkout consumption so a future template edit cannot silently drop it (the way `test_forkDispatch.js` pins the declaration).
- **AC4** — The factory reusable workflow declares `checkout_ref` (no undeclared `with:` input — GitHub fails reusable-workflow calls with unexpected inputs).

## Goal — a dispatched fork leg actually works the PR head tree (v1)

One sentence: **the leg's checkout consumes `inputs.checkout_ref`** — a gh-1075 fork-PR dispatch rides the base machine ref (`main`) and carries `refs/pull/<N>/head` in `inputs.checkout_ref`; the leg's checkout step must resolve that ref instead of the dispatch ref, so review/rework legs examine the fork PR's actual changes — not the base tree.

## Why this card exists (gh-1075 review thread, round 2)

gh-1075 (#1075 / PR #1089) made cross-repo PRs dispatchable: the dispatch reroutes onto `main` and DECLARES `checkout_ref` in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (declaration was required — GitHub 422s undeclared dispatch inputs, github/gh-aw#50027). Consumption was deferred, and the deferral named the #1074 lane. Review verified against the #1074 card text: #1074 is scoped **failure observability only** ("Non-goals: changing failure semantics") — it does NOT own a checkout-behavior change. So the consumption has no owner until this card.

The failure mode without it is silent wrong-tree work: a fork leg checks out `main`, produces green review/rework runs against the base code, and the fork PR's actual changes are never examined — no error anywhere (AC1 of gh-1075 "the leg's checkout step resolves refs/pull/<N>/head" stays unmet end-to-end).

## Scope

- The **template** `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` checkout step: when `inputs.checkout_ref != ''`, check out that ref (`git fetch origin <checkout_ref> && git checkout FETCH_HEAD`, or `gh pr checkout <N>`) instead of the dispatch ref. The placeholder `teammate` job documents the adaptation point; the machine-kit reference workflow (epam/dmtools-dart) carries the working runner steps and needs the same change.
- The **self-host stub** path: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` delegates to `IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml` — the factory reusable workflow must declare a `checkout_ref` input and consume it in its checkout step (sibling repo change; track here).
- The **rework push-back** targets the fork per the gh-1070 maintainer-edit contract (push to the fork's token URL, never the base branch).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A leg dispatched with `inputs.checkout_ref = refs/pull/<N>/head` checks out the PR head sha; the leg's git ops (diff, review, rework edits) run against the fork head tree.
- **AC2** — Same-repo dispatches (no `checkout_ref`) are byte-identical: checkout resolves the dispatch ref as today (REG guard).
- **AC3** — The rework leg's push-back lands on the fork (gh-1070 `forkPushTokenUrl` idiom), and a lint/unit assertion pins the checkout consumption so a future template edit cannot silently drop it (the way `test_forkDispatch.js` pins the declaration).
- **AC4** — The factory reusable workflow declares `checkout_ref` (no undeclared `with:` input — GitHub fails reusable-workflow calls with unexpected inputs).

## Test plan

- UT-1: template lint — the checkout step references `github.event.inputs.checkout_ref` and is guarded by `!= ''`.
- UT-2: a rendered checkout command for a fork dispatch names `refs/pull/<N>/head`.
- REG-1: existing gh-1075 fork-dispatch suites (dispatch reroute, probe, park) stay green.

## Non-goals

- The gh-1075 dispatch reroute itself (merged in PR #1089).
- The `validate_pr` CI-lane fork reroute (fork-blind lane; tracked separately, see the gh-1075 AC2 fork-blind notice).

## Live context

## Goal — a dispatched fork leg actually works the PR head tree (v1)

One sentence: **the leg's checkout consumes `inputs.checkout_ref`** — a gh-1075 fork-PR dispatch rides the base machine ref (`main`) and carries `refs/pull/<N>/head` in `inputs.checkout_ref`; the leg's checkout step must resolve that ref instead of the dispatch ref, so review/rework legs examine the fork PR's actual changes — not the base tree.

## Why this card exists (gh-1075 review thread, round 2)

gh-1075 (#1075 / PR #1089) made cross-repo PRs dispatchable: the dispatch reroutes onto `main` and DECLARES `checkout_ref` in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (declaration was required — GitHub 422s undeclared dispatch inputs, github/gh-aw#50027). Consumption was deferred, and the deferral named the #1074 lane. Review verified against the #1074 card text: #1074 is scoped **failure observability only** ("Non-goals: changing failure semantics") — it does NOT own a checkout-behavior change. So the consumption has no owner until this card.

The failure mode without it is silent wrong-tree work: a fork leg checks out `main`, produces green review/rework runs against the base code, and the fork PR's actual changes are never examined — no error anywhere (AC1 of gh-1075 "the leg's checkout step resolves refs/pull/<N>/head" stays unmet end-to-end).

## Scope

- The **template** `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` checkout step: when `inputs.checkout_ref != ''`, check out that ref (`git fetch origin <checkout_ref> && git checkout FETCH_HEAD`, or `gh pr checkout <N>`) instead of the dispatch ref. The placeholder `teammate` job documents the adaptation point; the machine-kit reference workflow (epam/dmtools-dart) carries the working runner steps and needs the same change.
- The **self-host stub** path: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` delegates to `IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml` — the factory reusable workflow must declare a `checkout_ref` input and consume it in its checkout step (sibling repo change; track here).
- The **rework push-back** targets the fork per the gh-1070 maintainer-edit contract (push to the fork's token URL, never the base branch).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A leg dispatched with `inputs.checkout_ref = refs/pull/<N>/head` checks out the PR head sha; the leg's git ops (diff, review, rework edits) run against the fork head tree.
- **AC2** — Same-repo dispatches (no `checkout_ref`) are byte-identical: checkout resolves the dispatch ref as today (REG guard).
- **AC3** — The rework leg's push-back lands on the fork (gh-1070 `forkPushTokenUrl` idiom), and a lint/unit assertion pins the checkout consumption so a future template edit cannot silently drop it (the way `test_forkDispatch.js` pins the declaration).
- **AC4** — The factory reusable workflow declares `checkout_ref` (no undeclared `with:` input — GitHub fails reusable-workflow calls with unexpected inputs).

## Test plan

- UT-1: template lint — the checkout step references `github.event.inputs.checkout_ref` and is guarded by `!= ''`.
- UT-2: a rendered checkout command for a fork dispatch names `refs/pull/<N>/head`.
- REG-1: existing gh-1075 fork-dispatch suites (dispatch reroute, probe, park) stay green.

## Non-goals

- The gh-1075 dispatch reroute itself (merged in PR #1089).
- The `validate_pr` CI-lane fork reroute (fork-blind lane; tracked separately, see the gh-1075 AC2 fork-blind notice).

## Live context

# Fixed — the probe names the TARGET repo, authenticated

You were right, and the round-1 `origin` suggestion is withdrawn in code too: in the SM's runtime `origin` is the **engine** repo (the gh-1070 silent-update comment at js/smAgent.js:2049-2051 documents it live-verified), so the probe would have asked the wrong repository on every non-self-host SM — AC2 inverted, exactly the damage you describe.

## Changes

- `js/smAgent.js::forkPullRefLive` now probes the target repo named by `repoInfo` with the established split-literal token URL idiom: `validationLiveness.forkPushTokenUrl('<owner>/<repo>')` → `git ls-remote https://x-access-token:` + `${GH_TOKEN}` + `@github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git refs/pull/<N>/head`. `${GH_TOKEN}` interpolates in the child env exactly like the existing silent-update commands, so the secret never appears contiguously in source or the captured command string.
- The DEGRADED fail-open catch is kept and now names both the pull ref and the probed repo (`fork pull-ref probe DEGRADED for refs/pull/<N>/head (pr-<N>, <owner>/<repo> probe failed: …)`).
- Comment block rewritten to record the engine-checkout rationale.

## Tests (flipped as you asked)

- `test_smAgent.js` — the `origin` test now asserts the probe command names `epam/dmtools-dart` from `repoInfo`, rides the `x-access-token:${GH_TOKEN}@github.com/` URL (asserted with the codebase's split-literal `TOK` idiom), and contains no ` ls-remote origin `.
- The private-repo-shaped DEGRADED test stays green: auth failure → fail-open LIVE, distinct greppable warning naming the PR, no markers, no park.
- Full gh-1075 suite green (628 `run_smAgent` tests via the canonical dmtools runner).

## Goal — a dispatched fork leg actually works the PR head tree (v1)

One sentence: **the leg's checkout consumes `inputs.checkout_ref`** — a gh-1075 fork-PR dispatch rides the base machine ref (`main`) and carries `refs/pull/<N>/head` in `inputs.checkout_ref`; the leg's checkout step must resolve that ref instead of the dispatch ref, so review/rework legs examine the fork PR's actual changes — not the base tree.

## Why this card exists (gh-1075 review thread, round 2)

gh-1075 (#1075 / PR #1089) made cross-repo PRs dispatchable: the dispatch reroutes onto `main` and DECLARES `checkout_ref` in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (declaration was required — GitHub 422s undeclared dispatch inputs, github/gh-aw#50027). Consumption was deferred, and the deferral named the #1074 lane. Review verified against the #1074 card text: #1074 is scoped **failure observability only** ("Non-goals: changing failure semantics") — it does NOT own a checkout-behavior change. So the consumption has no owner until this card.

The failure mode without it is silent wrong-tree work: a fork leg checks out `main`, produces green review/rework runs against the base code, and the fork PR's actual changes are never examined — no error anywhere (AC1 of gh-1075 "the leg's checkout step resolves refs/pull/<N>/head" stays unmet end-to-end).

## Scope

- The **template** `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` checkout step: when `inputs.checkout_ref != ''`, check out that ref (`git fetch origin <checkout_ref> && git checkout FETCH_HEAD`, or `gh pr checkout <N>`) instead of the dispatch ref. The placeholder `teammate` job documents the adaptation point; the machine-kit reference workflow (epam/dmtools-dart) carries the working runner steps and needs the same change.
- The **self-host stub** path: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` delegates to `IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml` — the factory reusable workflow must declare a `checkout_ref` input and consume it in its checkout step (sibling repo change; track here).
- The **rework push-back** targets the fork per the gh-1070 maintainer-edit contract (push to the fork's token URL, never the base branch).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — A leg dispatched with `inputs.checkout_ref = refs/pull/<N>/head` checks out the PR head sha; the leg's git ops (diff, review, rework edits) run against the fork head tree.
- **AC2** — Same-repo dispatches (no `checkout_ref`) are byte-identical: checkout resolves the dispatch ref as today (REG guard).
- **AC3** — The rework leg's push-back lands on the fork (gh-1070 `forkPushTokenUrl` idiom), and a lint/unit assertion pins the checkout consumption so a future template edit cannot silently drop it (the way `test_forkDispatch.js` pins the declaration).
- **AC4** — The factory reusable workflow declares `checkout_ref` (no undeclared `with:` input — GitHub fails reusable-workflow calls with unexpected inputs).

## Test plan

- UT-1: template lint — the checkout step references `github.event.inputs.checkout_ref` and is guarded by `!= ''`.
- UT-2: a rendered checkout command for a fork dispatch names `refs/pull/<N>/head`.
- REG-1: existing gh-1075 fork-dispatch suites (dispatch reroute, probe, park) stay green.

## Non-goals

- The gh-1075 dispatch reroute itself (merged in PR #1089).
- The `validate_pr` CI-lane fork reroute (fork-blind lane; tracked separately, see the gh-1075 AC2 fork-blind notice).

## Live context

# Fixed — the self-host stub run-name now renders `· pr-<N>`

Took the first fix option (template the anchor into the stub's run-name under the gh-1065 leg-title contract), plus the drift guard you asked for.

## Changes

- `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` — `run-name` now renders the whole-token pr anchor right after the issue slot, **before** the trailing-leg token:

  `teammate: <event> #<issue> · pr-<N> <leg>` whenever `inputs.pr` is set (guarded by `(github.event.inputs.pr || '') != ''` — the `null != ''` trap the template comment documents; on issues events the anchor renders nothing and titles are byte-identical to today).
- The anchor deliberately sits **before** the leg: `stubTailLegOf` (`/\s(dev|review|rework)$/`, js/common/teammateEventDedup.js:193) parses the leg at the END of the title, and the gh-1065 completed-owner leg precision depends on it. Appending after the leg would have blinded `legOfRunName` exactly when the gh-1075 fork gate needs both.

One sentence: **the leg's checkout consumes `inputs.checkout_ref`** — a gh-1075 fork-PR dispatch rides the base machine ref (`main`) and carries `refs/pull/<N>/head` in `inputs.checkout_ref`; the leg's checkout step must resolve that ref instead of the dispatch ref, so review/rework legs examine the fork PR's actual changes — not the base tree.

## Why this card exists (gh-1075 review thread, round 2)

gh-1075 (#1075 / PR #1089) made cross-repo PRs dispatchable: the dispatch reroutes onto `main` and DECLARES `checkout_ref` in `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` (declaration was required — GitHub 422s undeclared dispatch inputs, github/gh-aw#50027). So the consumption has no owner until this card.

The failure mode without it is silent wrong-tree work: a fork leg checks out `main`, produces green review/rework runs against the base code, and the fork PR's actual changes are never examined — no error anywhere (AC1 of gh-1075 "the leg's checkout step resolves refs/pull/<N>/head" stays unmet end-to-end).

- The **template** `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` checkout step: when `inputs.checkout_ref != ''`, check out that ref (`git fetch origin <checkout_ref> && git checkout FETCH_HEAD`, or `gh pr checkout <N>`) instead of the dispatch ref. # Confirmed against the card text — consumption was NOT tracked; the tracking card now exists (#1096)

You were right to push on this: I pulled the actual #1074 card and its **Non-goals** state *"Changing failure semantics — this card is observability only."* Checkout behavior is out of #1074's scope, so the gh-1075 deferral named the wrong lane.

## What this pass did about it

- **Filed the tracking card: [IstiN/dmtools-agents#1096](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/issues/1096)** — "[GOAL] Fork leg consumes inputs.checkout_ref", with ACs covering: the leg checkout resolving `refs/pull/<N>/head` (AC1), byte-identical same-repo behavior (AC2), the rework push-back targeting the fork per the gh-1070 contract plus a lint assertion pinning consumption (AC3), and the factory reusable workflow declaring the input (AC4). It also scopes the sibling-repo change (the factory `factory-teammate.yml` owns the self-host checkout) and the template/machine-kit adaptation point.
- `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template` — the `checkout_ref` description now names #1096 as the consumption owner instead of "#1074", so the contract text in the shipped template no longer points at a lane whose non-goals exclude it.
- `test_forkDispatch.js` lint-suite comment updated to match.

## Why consumption itself is not implemented in this pass

The actual checkout runs in code this PR does not own: the self-host stub delegates to `IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml` (a reusable-workflow `with:` call — passing an undeclared input there fails hard), and the template's `teammate` job is a documented adaptation placeholder whose working runner steps live in the machine-kit reference (epam/dmtools-dart). Implementing consumption here would either be a no-op placeholder edit or a cross-repo change beyond this lane — exactly what #1096 now tracks with testable ACs.

So: the silent wrong-tree failure mode you describe is now an explicitly owned, AC'd card rather than an implicit deferral, and AC1's end-to-end claim is no longer made by this lane until #1096 lands.

{"content":"# Fixed — the probe names the TARGET repo, authenticated

You were right, and the round-1 `origin` suggestion is withdrawn in code too: in the SM's runtime `origin` is the **engine** repo (the gh-1070 silent-update comment at js/smAgent.js:2049-2051 documents it live-verified), so the probe would have asked the wrong repository on every non-self-host SM — AC2 inverted, exactly the damage you describe.

## Changes

- `js/smAgent.js::forkPullRefLive` now probes the target repo named by `repoInfo` with the established split-literal token URL idiom: `validationLiveness.forkPushTokenUrl('<owner>/<repo>')` → `git ls-remote https://x-access-token:` + `${GH_TOKEN}` + `@github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git refs/pull/<N>/head`. `${GH_TOKEN}` interpolates in the child env exactly like the existing silent-update commands, so the secret never appears contiguously in source or the captured command string.

# AI Teammate — GitHub-issues machine runner (TEMPLATE).
#
# Copy into the TARGET repository (.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml) and
# adapt the RUNNER_* entries. This is the trimmed generic variant of the
# battle-tested machine-kit workflow (see epam/dmtools-dart
# .github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml for the full reference with comments).
#
# Two entry paths, and BOTH must survive for the loop to be self-healing:
#   1. issues: [assigned, labeled] — the fast path (labels added with a
#      real PAT fire events; GITHUB_TOKEN-added labels do NOT — that is
#      exactly what the SM cron covers)
#   2. workflow_dispatch (issue / leg / reason) — the SM dispatch path:
#      the reconciler fires this directly, so mute labels cannot stall the
#      loop
#
# The guard derives the leg: dispatch input leg > label agent:rework >
# label agent:review > assignee/agent:dev (dev). Each leg runs the dmtools
# agent config named by RUNNER_*: dev (story/bug) develops from the issue
# body, review produces a machine PR review verdict, rework fixes the
# linked PR by the review threads.
#
# gh-1065/gh-1073: issues events are deduped before the leg fires — one
# human action (assign, or assign-while-labels-change) emits MULTIPLE
# issues events, and without the `dedup` probe job each event spawned its
# own teammate run (live 2026-10-18: #1040–#1043 two runs each, #1061
# three). The probe is transport only; the decision is the unit-tested
# pure module js/common/teammateEventDedup.js, shipped in the agents pack
# the runner leg mounts (dmtools-agents checkout). The probe FAILS OPEN on
# errors, so a broken check never swallows the only trigger.
name: 'AI Teammate'

# Run title carries the EFFECTIVE anchor (owner 2026-09-27, live: dmd run
# 36333172145): a PR-anchored SM dispatch (#544/#687 — inputs.pr set,
# inputs.issue empty) must title '▶ rework (SM) · pr-266', never the
# malformed '▶ rework (SM) · gh- · gh-: '. (inputs.pr || '') guards the
# label-event path, where inputs are null — null != '' would be TRUE and
# render 'pr-' for ordinary issue events.
#
# gh-1065/gh-1073: the issues-event title ALSO carries the LEG — the
# strongest arming label on the issue (rework > review > pr_approved →
# review > dev), not the label written by THIS event: assign-while-labels-
# change emits a bare `assigned` event whose github.event.label.name is
# empty. legOfRunName (js/common/teammateEventDedup.js) parses this emoji
# title family, so a COMPLETED owner stays title-precise: the strict
# completed-owner leg rule (a leg-less completed run never swallows a
# KNOWN new leg) can only work when real leg runs carry their leg here.
run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework') ||
      (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review') ||
      (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'pr_approved') && '🔍 review') ||
      (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:dev') && '⚒️ dev') ||
      (contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:develop') && '⚒️ dev') ||
      github.event.label.name || '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (#544/#687) — the SM dispatches review/rework with pr instead of issue when the PR has no resolvable LOCAL issue; gh-1075 fork-PR dispatches always backfill it so the run title carries the · pr-<N> anchor'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      checkout_ref:
        description: 'gh-1075 fork-PR dispatch: the leg checks out this ref (refs/pull/<N>/head — always fetchable on the base repo, even when the fork branch is deleted) instead of the dispatch ref. DECLARED here because GitHub 422s undeclared dispatch inputs ("Unexpected inputs provided"); consumption lives in the #1074 leg-checkout lane.'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  actions: write

env:
  AGENT_HANDLE: ai-teammate
  # ── adapt per target repo ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  RUNNER_STORY: dmtools-agents/story_development.json
  RUNNER_BUG: dmtools-agents/bug_development.json
  RUNNER_REVIEW: dmtools-agents/pr_review.json
  RUNNER_REWORK: dmtools-agents/pr_rework.json
  DMTOOLS_AGENTS_REF: main
  DMTOOLS_VERSION: v0.1.5
  FA_VERSION: latest
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Secrets expected: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (PAT), plus the AI provider key
  # referenced by the runner configs (e.g. ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY).

jobs:
  guard:
    # gh-1029: the `labeled` trigger fires on EVERY label write — including
    # the leg's own lifecycle labels (status:*, ai_developed, ...) — and
    # `on:` cannot filter by label name. Without this job-level gate the
    # guard allocated a runner on each lifecycle-label write only to decide
    # run=false (the self-retrigger no-op burn). `assigned` and the arming
    # `labeled` events (agent:*) still enter; lifecycle labels skip the job
    # entirely and never allocate a runner.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'assigned') ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.action == 'labeled' &&
       (github.event.label.name == 'agent:dev' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:develop' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' ||
        github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

[GOAL] update_branch failures must log the stderr tail (git rejection reason) — 3-failure streak on fa #1591 is undebuggable from run logs
---BODY---
## Goal — silent-update failures surface the stderr TAIL, so fork-push rejections are debuggable after the fact (v1)

One sentence: **a failed `update_branch` reports why git said no** — the error surface carries the stderr tail, where git writes the actual rejection — instead of only the command's opening lines.

Live incident: fa PR #1591, 2026-10-19 05:51/05:52Z — the fork silent-update push failed 3 times with `maintainerCanModify: true` (push should have succeeded), and the SM run log preserved only "Cloning into '…' / Updating files: N%" — the beginning of stderr. The rejection reason (hook declined? permission mapping? branch-create restriction?) is unrecoverable; the PR had to be rescued manually and the root cause of the streak is still unknown.

## Root cause

`update_branch` failures propagate `cli_execute_command`'s exception, whose message embeds the command output from the START (head-truncated). Git writes progress to stderr continuously and the decisive error ("remote: error: …", "To <url> ! [remote rejected] HEAD:branch (reason)") at the END — exactly the part that is cut.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — On any `update_branch` failure (silent-update lane, same-repo and fork paths), the propagated error/log entry includes the LAST ~20 lines of stderr, not (only) the head.
- **AC2** — The failure bookkeeping comment on the PR (`silent-update failure — attempt N`) gains a one-line reason extracted from the tail (e.g. the `remote rejected … (reason)` fragment) when present — the PR timeline alone explains the streak.
- **AC3** — Secrets hygiene: the tail is scrubbed with the same token-redaction the command line already gets (assert by test with a token-shaped string in a fake tail).
- **AC4** — Same-repo lane unchanged in behavior except the error text (regression guard on existing silent-update suites).

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — fake cli failure with a long stderr: propagated message contains the tail lines, not just the head.
- `UT-2` — rejection-reason extraction from a realistic git push refusal tail (fixture).
- `UT-3` — token-shaped string in the fake tail is redacted (AC3).
- `REG-1` — existing silent-update failure-bookkeeping tests (attempt counting, degraded flag) stay green.

## Non-goals

- Changing failure semantics (attempt counting, guest-park fallback per #1070 AC3) — this card is observability only.
- Full stdout/stderr capture for every cli_execute_command call (scoped to the update_branch failure path).

Confirmed: #1074 is scoped as failure observability ("observability only", "Non-goals: changing failure semantics"). # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).
